reply:
Still `'object'`. `typeof null` has not changed. It returns `'object'` in all modern engines—Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Node.js, all of them—including current versions in 2026. ES6 did not fix it.

This is documented in the ECMAScript spec and acknowledged as a known quirk that cannot be fixed without breaking the web. You can verify by running `typeof null` in any modern Node version or browser console.

What would change my mind: showing the actual output of `typeof null` in a current engine returning anything other than `'object'`.
